title: Intervals: merge by start
summary: Merge overlapping closed intervals. Sort by start; a start past the last merged end opens a new interval, otherwise extend that end. Touching intervals merge, hence '>'. O(n log n).
code: # Sort first, then compare with the last merged interval.
if not merged or start > merged[-1][1]:
triggers: overlapping ranges, bookings or time blocks
merge, insert into, or find conflicts among intervals
prompts: A calendar export lists busy blocks in random order, some overlapping. Produce the fewest blocks that cover exactly the same busy time.
Several edits highlighted overlapping character ranges in a document. Collapse them into separate, non-overlapping ranges before drawing.
invariant: merged is sorted, pairwise disjoint, and covers exactly the intervals seen so far.
mantra: Sort by start; an overlap stretches the last end, a gap opens a new interval.
pitfalls: Closed intervals that touch ([1, 2] and [2, 3]) merge, so the test is start > end, not >=.
Extend with max(): an interval inside the last one must not shrink it.
Append a fresh [start, end]; editing an input list changes the caller's data.
